change.title: pr-36882-flat
change.description: Add rolling-updates feature flag and compatibility framework
change.author: Cristian Sotomayor

findings.title: Doc says the Operator fails without `rolling-updates`, but nothing in the Operator checks the feature
findings.body: The caution says the Operator "will fail" if `rolling-updates` is not enabled. The Operator never reads that feature. `UpgradeLogicFactory.create` (operator/src/main/java/org/keycloak/operator/upgrade/UpgradeLogicFactory.java:35-43) picks an upgrade logic from `spec.update.strategy` alone. No code under operator/src/main mentions `rolling-updates` or calls `update-compatibility`. `UpgradeTest` shows this too: with a `null` strategy it leaves the feature off (UpgradeTest.java:105-107) and still expects the upgrades to work. So the only thing gated today is the `update-compatibility` CLI. Either reword the caution, for example to say the feature will be required once the Operator uses the compatibility check, or add the gate to the Operator.

findings.title: Enabling the feature here changes nothing the Operator does, and the list replaces any features already set
findings.body: No Operator code depends on `ROLLING_UPDATES`, so turning it on only in the `RECREATE` branch tests nothing new. Its only effect is to put a build-time option on the CR. `setEnabledFeatures(List.of(...))` also overwrites whatever `getTestKeycloakDeployment` may already have put in `enabledFeatures`, instead of adding to it. Either drop the change until the Operator actually uses the feature, or append to the existing list.

findings.title: Hard-coded `--features=rolling-updates` in a shared macro
findings.body: The `updatecompatibility` macro now adds `--features=rolling-updates` to every example. A user who already enables other features with `--features` or in `keycloak.conf` will copy an example where this flag replaces their feature list, so the options no longer match their deployment. That defeats a tool whose job is comparing configurations. Consider saying in the prose (the CAUTION block already does this) that the feature must be enabled along with the user's existing features, and not forcing the flag inside the macro.

findings.title: Feature key hard-coded in the error message
findings.body: Build the message from `Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES.getKey()` instead of the literal `'rolling-updates'`, so the message stays correct if the feature is renamed. UpgradeTest already does this.

contracts.action: update-compatibility check/metadata now refuse to run unless the ROLLING_UPDATES feature is enabled, and exit with code 4
contracts.equivalent_path: Other uses of Profile.isFeatureEnabled, e.g. common/src/main/java/org/keycloak/common/util/MultiSiteUtils.java:25. The profile is set up in PropertyMappers.sanitizeDisabledMappers when a command is parsed.
contracts.before_after: Profile.isFeatureEnabled dereferences Profile.getInstance() (common/src/main/java/org/keycloak/common/Profile.java:408-410). For a parsed command, the profile is initialised through Environment.getCurrentOrCreateFeatureProfile before run() is called, so the check sees the user's --features.
contracts.visible_effect: An error line on stderr and exit code 4. The documentation table now lists 4 as feature disabled, and the recreate code changes from 4 to 3, which matches the table the docs already had.
contracts.failure_mode: If the profile were not initialised, the check would throw an NPE. That does not happen here because sanitizeDisabledMappers runs whenever a command is present.

contracts.action: Operator docs and test enable rolling-updates on the Keycloak CR
contracts.equivalent_path: UpgradeLogicFactory picks the upgrade logic from the strategy only
contracts.before_after: The Operator never checks the feature, so behaviour is the same with or without it.
contracts.visible_effect: None in Operator behaviour. The docs claim it will fail, which is not true.

summary: This PR adds a preview feature, `rolling-updates`, and makes the `update-compatibility` commands require it. Disabled-feature runs now exit with code 4, and the recreate exit code moves from 4 to 3. The new code matches the exit-code table the docs already had. The CLI check works because the profile is already set up when a command is parsed. I found nothing that blocks the merge; all four findings are at "consider". The Operator docs claim the Operator fails without the feature, but the Operator never checks it. The UpgradeTest change enables a feature the Operator ignores, and it replaces any features already set instead of adding to them. The shared docs macro hard-codes `--features=rolling-updates`, which would wipe a user's own feature list if they copy an example. The feature key is hard-coded in the error message.
